items.question: Why does DeepWalk’s use of edge weights help it outperform LINE on the language network so strongly?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk uses edge weights and therefore outperforms LINE on the language network.
items.correction: DeepWalk has to ignore edge weights, and LINE with edge-sampling performs very well on the language network.
items.evidence_quote: This is because DeepWalk has to ignore the weights (i.e., co-occurrences) of the edges, which is very important in a language network.

items.question: How does LINE improve document embeddings by optimizing them directly for the best document classification accuracy?
items.false_premise: LINE is used to directly optimize document embeddings for the best classification performance.
items.correction: The document vectors are obtained by averaging word vectors, because the goal is to compare word embeddings rather than find the best document embedding method.
items.evidence_quote: This is because we aim to compare the word embeddings with different approaches instead of finding the best method for document embeddings.

items.question: What makes LINE-SGD faster than graph factorization when it is trained with ordinary SGD on the language network?
items.false_premise: LINE-SGD is trained with ordinary SGD and is faster than graph factorization.
items.correction: LINE optimized by edge-sampling is the efficient variant, LINE-SGDs are slightly slower, and both LINE(1st) and LINE(2nd) are at least 10% faster than graph factorization.
items.evidence_quote: The LINE optimized by the edge-sampling treatment effectively addresses this problem, and performs very well using either first-order or second-order proximity.

items.question: Under which conditions does DeepWalk become the faster method, given that it is about five times quicker than LINE on the large language network?
items.false_premise: DeepWalk is faster than LINE on the large language network.
items.correction: LINE is much more efficient than DeepWalk, and DeepWalk is five times slower.
items.evidence_quote: Both are at least 10% faster than graph factorization, and much more efficient than DeepWalk (five times slower).
